page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized, network-optimized fifth-generation server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 3.1 GHz. The CPU includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX-512_VNNI. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This instance does not include local storage, relying entirely on network-attached EBS storage. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth (reaching 87.18 GB/sec for large uncached blocks), and database operations scale to average middle-tier levels.

The r5n.4xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded performance. Its high memory density and enhanced network throughput make it well-suited for distributed in-memory databases like Redis, which achieves 13.18 million operations per second in benchmarks. It is also appropriate for medium-scale database hosting, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM without the overhead of local NVMe storage.
